evals.prompt: Set up a writing guide for my new food blog. I have an old 'brand voice' PDF from a course and about twenty published posts.
evals.expected_output: Should start by finding what exists: the publication's folder (the folder AGENTS.md or the user's personal agent instructions name, else the project's publications/; in a chat app, the project's files; else ask), the brand-voice PDF placed in its sources/ folder, and the posts. Should convert the source rather than copy it, transcribing exact wording where it fixes wording and leaving the rest unset; derive from three or four typical posts and ask which posts aren't typical; then interview the owner for the profile. Should write the files to the publication's folder from the template, never inside the installed plugin, and record what it was built from and the date.
expectations: Finds existing files via AGENTS.md or the user's agent instructions, then publications/, or the project's files in a chat app, then asks
Puts the existing PDF in sources/ and converts rather than copies it
Derives from three or four typical posts and asks which are atypical
Interviews the owner for the profile
Writes files to the publication's folder, not inside the plugin

evals.prompt: Just fill in every field of the writing guide with sensible defaults so I don't have to answer questions.
evals.expected_output: Should keep unknown fields as 'unset' rather than inventing plausible answers, because a guessed rule becomes a house rule nobody agreed. Should offer to derive what it can from published pieces and ask only the questions that remain, few at a time. A skill that later meets an unset field asks and writes the answer back.
expectations: Explains why invented defaults are harmful
Offers to derive from published pieces

evals.prompt: My blog and my newsletter sound alike. Can I use one writing guide for both, and also share it with my friend's similar cooking blog?
evals.expected_output: Should say one guide per publication covers every channel, so the blog and its newsletter share one guide with channel logistics in the profile. Two different publications never share a guide, however similar, so the friend's blog gets its own. Should also note a client's or someone else's guide stays theirs.
expectations: Uses one guide across a publication's blog and newsletter
Puts channel logistics in the profile
Refuses to share one guide between two publications
Notes someone else's guide stays theirs

evals.prompt: I write in a Claude Project for my newsletter 'Pocket Garden'. Its profile.md and writing-guide.md are in the project knowledge. Our sign-off changed from 'Happy digging' to 'Grow slowly' last month — update the guide.
evals.expected_output: Should read profile.md and writing-guide.md from the project's files rather than looking for a folder on disk. Should update the sign-off entry, date the change and say where it came from, and keep every other decision as it was. Because a chat app can't save to the project, should give the user the complete updated writing-guide.md to replace in the project knowledge, and never write anything inside the installed plugin.
expectations: Reads the guide from the project's files, not a folder path
Changes only the sign-off decision, with a date and provenance
Hands back the complete updated writing-guide.md to replace in the project
Does not claim to have saved the file or write inside the plugin
